properties.name: Agent-to-agent feedback is written for reproduction, not for brevity — and the human whose project it was written inside still decides whether it leaves
properties.statement:
ANTHONY, 2026-08-14, settling the two constraints on agent-authored feedback while the DELIVERY mechanism stays open on `dec:idea-agent-to-agent-feedback-is-a-formal-channel`. Both were raised as counters to his own proposal and he agreed with both.

═══ 1 · THE CONSENT BOUNDARY — who may be cut out, and who may not ═══

**TWO DIFFERENT HUMANS ARE IN THIS LOOP AND ONLY ONE MAY BE REMOVED.**
  · **THE ROUTING HUMAN** — the person who today must read an agent's friction note, understand it, and relay it onward. Pure overhead. **Removing them is the point of the whole idea.**
  · **THE CONSENTING HUMAN** — the person whose project the feedback was written INSIDE. **Not removable.**

HIS WORDS: *"the agent writes freely for another agent; the human still decides whether it leaves."*

⇒ WHAT THIS REQUIRES: an agent may compose feedback for another agent without a human in the authoring loop, at any length and in any form useful to a machine reader. **Nothing may transmit it off the machine it was written on without that project's owner deciding.** A channel that ships unasked is an exfiltration path however good the intent, because the material was produced inside someone else's design.

📌 THE DISCIPLINE ALREADY EXISTS AND WAS HONOURED UNPROMPTED IN THE FIELD. `report-friction` redacts the user's design content and never files without asking; the Grok 4.6 feedback file of 2026-08-13 wrote its own guard rail: *"Per report-friction: do not open a public issue without asking. This file is the local log."* and *"Product/design content is summarized by type and count, not quoted."* **This requirement does not invent that restraint — it says the new channel may not lose it.** `req:telemetry-carries-usage-never-design-content` is the standing rule it inherits.

📌 CONSENT IS SEPARATELY MODELLED AND UNBUILT: `dec:idea-feedback-collection-is-asked-once-and-recorded` — asked for by Alex himself — decides WHETHER feedback may travel. This requirement decides that it may not travel without that answer.

═══ 2 · THE FORMAT TARGET — reproducibility, not terseness ═══

HIS WORDS: *"The target should be reproducibility, not terseness."*

⇒ WHAT THIS REQUIRES: agent-authored feedback is written so a receiving agent can RE-RUN the claim, not merely read it. Each report names the tool, the arguments, the observed result, the expected result, and — explicitly — **what the author did not check.**

🛑 THE EVIDENCE, AND IT IS WHY THE OBVIOUS OPTIMISATION IS WRONG. The stated appeal of a machine-to-machine channel is that it can *"be very efficient and remove any fluff that is needed when a human is in the loop."* **But brevity is not what made the 2026-08-13 file valuable.** Four of its items were independently reproduced by a different agent on a different graph within a day (`fact:agent-feedback-corroborated-2026-08-14`), and every one of the four was reproducible **because it named the tool and its arguments**: `get_node({node_type: Project, id: "proj:…"})` returning `{node: null}` could be re-run in a single call and confirmed. Its items that were only narrated could not be checked at all.

⚠️ **A FORMAT OPTIMISED FOR COMPACTNESS WOULD DELETE EXACTLY THE PARTS THAT WORKED.** The same file carried a *"Gaps (mine / process)"* section admitting it had skipped `compare_designs`, guessed a Project id, and not exported after writing. That self-reporting reads as overhead and is the first thing terseness removes — yet it is what tells a reader which claims are load-bearing and which are unexamined.

⚠️ AND THE CONFIRMED/UNCONFIRMED SPLIT MUST BE STRUCTURAL, not left to the writer's conscience. That file's `get_instructions` truncation report did NOT reproduce here — the payload arrived complete — which was only discoverable because the claim was specific enough to test. A report that cannot be tested cannot be disconfirmed either, and an untestable claim that hardens into folklore is the failure `dec:idea-intent-crosses-designs` already recorded once about this project.

═══ WHAT THIS REQUIREMENT DOES NOT SETTLE ═══

The mechanism is open on `dec:idea-agent-to-agent-feedback-is-a-formal-channel`: extend `report-friction` with an agent-to-agent mode, a new served skill, a structured field format, or leave it ad-hoc. **Option (d), a graph node type, is blocked by a real constraint** — the authoring agent works inside someone else's design, so the note must travel as a DOCUMENT rather than as a node.
